newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Chile spirits lifted by alcohol tax accord.
newsitem.headline: EU, Chile spirits lifted by alcohol tax accord.

text.p: The European Union and Chile have provisionally settled a long-running feud over alcohol tax, with Chile agreeing to harmonise tariffs on domestic and imported spirits, EU Commissioner Manuel Marin said on Thursday.

Marin told the European Parliament the Chilean authorities had agreed to alter by the end of April legislation which subjects imported spirits -- including Scotch whisky -- to higher rates of tax than the local spirit pisco.
He said that if Chile did not honour its promise, the EU would refer its complaint to a World Trade Organisation disputes panel.
"If we do not get an adequate response from the Chilean authorities, the European Union will automatically open up a panel in the (WTO)," the Spanish commissioner said.
Last year a WTO disputes panel ruled that Japanese taxes discriminated against European spirits exports.
Japan agreed in February to slash taxes on European spirits and raise taxes on domestic spirits.
The Japanese decision was welcomed by European spirits producers, who said in February they would press for similar changes in South Korea and Chile.
